newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Fin Min may extend tax relief for NFIs.
newsitem.headline: Polish Fin Min may extend tax relief for NFIs.

text.p: The Polish Finance Ministry may drop plans to scrap next year the tax exemption which the country's 15 National Investment Funds enjoy on gains from sales of firms from their portfolios, Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Monday.
Belka said the ministry might either issue a regulation extending the relief or propose a relevant amendment of the law on investment funds.

"There are two solutions: either to extend the relief through a resolution or include the relief in the law on investment funds," he told reporters. Under the current NFI and tax laws, the funds would have to pay the 36-percent corporate tax on revenues from sales of shares from their portfolios as of next year, which analysts said would make them unattractive for many investors.
Under the government's NFI programme, shares in more than 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.

From Monday, the 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in the scheme have the opportunity to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund, which are expected to start trade on the Warsaw bourse around mid-year.

The NFI units jumped nearly six percent to 151.5 zloty on Monday on news that the tax exemption for the funds may be extended and on recently published financial resuts, which showed most funds had a net profit in the first quarter of 1997. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
